The team identifies two binaries, with orbital periods of 87 and 67 minutes. In each, a brown dwarf steadily feeds mass onto an M dwarf companion. They argue such systems may be consumed slowly over billions of years instead of destroyed at once.
arxiv-2603-17139: Hudson, Charlin, and Frejinger learn distributions of human preferences for use in later decisions. Preferences vary between people and shift with context, which point estimates miss. Their pipeline trains a model that maps context features to a rich family of preference distributions, by maximum likelihood. The choice settings are framed as integer linear programs. The fitted model then generates scenarios for unseen contexts, feeding risk averse optimization. In a synthetic ridesharing test, their approach cut average post decision surprise sharply versus risk neutral and risk averse baselines.
arxiv-2603-17539: Muñoz González extends mean field game models of automated market makers. Earlier work by the same author covered traders alone, then traders with transaction costs. The new model adds liquidity providers and arbitrageurs as agent types. The provider acts as a dominating player whose choices shape the trader distribution. Arbitrageur impact enters through loss-versus-rebalancing. He offers the setup as an open research proposal, not closed results.
arxiv-2603-17639: Zhang and co-authors present VeriGrey, a greybox tester for language-model agents. Agents that call tools on their own can take rare but risky paths. VeriGrey uses the tool-call sequence as feedback to steer test search. Prompt mutations then hide an injection task inside the agent's own job. On AgentDojo it found a third more injection flaws than a black-box baseline, they report. Case studies hit a coding agent and a personal assistant.
arxiv-2603-17839: Kumaran and co-authors ask how language models form the confidence scores they state in words. Two options compete: compute on demand, or cache a self-judgment made while answering. Steering, patching, and swap tests on three models point to caching. Confidence signals gather from answer tokens and sit at the first post-answer spot, they find. Probes show those signals track answer quality past raw token odds. Stated confidence thus reflects built-in self-review.
arxiv-2603-18039: Nicholson studies sharpness aware surrogate training for spiking neural networks. Standard training pairs a nonsmooth forward model with a biased gradient estimate. The new scheme runs sharpness aware minimization on a smooth surrogate model instead. Its gradient is exact for that model, and theory gives stability and convergence bounds. On N-MNIST, hard spike accuracy rose from 65.7% to 94.7% while surrogate accuracy stayed high.
arxiv-2603-18139: Chiti and co-authors give the first spectropolarimetric time series for HD 166620, a Maunder Minimum analog star. Twelve nights of CFHT/SPIRou data plus one ESPaDOnS epoch show no clear signal in single profiles. A grand average profile, fit with a pure dipole model, gives a field near 1.10 gauss. That value matches solar dipole models for the Maunder Minimum. The result supports weakened magnetic braking through a weaker large-scale field.
arxiv-2603-18339: Graßl and co-authors map Norrish type-I reaction paths in acetophenone with ultrafast X-ray absorption. These reactions cleave bonds beside carbonyl groups and serve UV curing and additive manufacturing. Time-resolved near-edge spectra at the oxygen K-edge track the excited state flow. Population moves to the n-pi-star state in about 0.13 picoseconds after a short induction pause. It then crosses to a long-lived triplet state within about 3.17 picoseconds, matching simulations.
arxiv-2603-18439: Teng and co-authors study multipartite mutual information for bosonic and fermionic fields near a dilaton black hole. One observer hovers near the horizon of a Garfinkle-Horowitz-Strominger black hole; others stay far away. Tracing over hidden modes gives analytic forms for GHZ and W states. Fermionic mutual information exceeds the bosonic value under the Hawking effect. GHZ states also carry more mutual information than W states, while coherence orders reverse.
arxiv-2603-18639: Wang and co-authors build OrthoPhys to make generated videos obey basic physics. Video models see only flat views of motion that unfolds in 3D space. OrthoPhys first creates four synced orthogonal views of the moving subject. Cross-view attention enforces 3D coherence across those views. The steady subject then guides synthesis of the full scene with background. Training uses PhysMV, a new set of 40,000 scenes with four views each. Tests show clear gains in physical realism and space-time coherence over prior video methods.
arxiv-2603-18739: Liu and co-authors introduce EdgeCrafter, a compact vision transformer family for dense prediction on edge devices. Small ViTs often trail CNN models like YOLO under tight compute and memory limits. The team blames weak task-specific feature learning, not the transformer design itself. Their ECDet detector uses a distilled backbone with an edge-friendly encoder-decoder. The same features feed light heads for instance segmentation and pose estimation. The small detector reaches 51.7 box AP with under ten million parameters. Larger variants top 59.9 box AP after extra detection pre-training.
arxiv-2603-18939: Sarma and co-authors present a tool to check the safety of masked crypto hardware built by high-level synthesis. Masking guards chips against power-based side attacks. Synthesis tools were not built for security, so their tweaks can open leaks. Past checkers raise false alarms on shared control paths in such designs. Their tool checks the design state by state to avoid those false alarms. It correctly checks standard crypto tests, including cascaded masked parts and a masked PRESENT S-box.
arxiv-2603-19239: Bouras and Mechtaev help symbolic execution get past code blocks that stall constraint solvers. Their Gordian tool asks a language model to write small ghost code for the hard parts. Ghost code can flip a tough block, swap in a solver-friendly stand-in, or split a heap space. The solver keeps charge of the full, exact reasoning. Built on KLEE, it lifts code coverage by 28 to 115 percent over classic tools. It also cuts language model token use by over 90 percent.
arxiv-2603-19339: Li and co-authors shrink the vectors used in dense passage search without losing much quality. Cutting dimensions saves space, but classic methods waste capacity or boost noise. Their SpecTemp sets a scaling power for each target size from the data spectrum itself. Local signal-to-noise checks and a knee rule fix the value, with no labels needed. Across tests, scores stay near the best that a grid search can find. The method is learning-free and works across models. Code for the approach is public on GitHub.
arxiv-2603-19839: Miyatsu, Cheoun, and Saito study quarkyonic matter inside a relativistic quark model. They merge the dual quarkyonic picture with the quark-meson coupling model. The combined QQMC model uses relativistic Gaussian quark wavefunctions for the nucleon. They study symmetric nuclear matter and pure neutron matter with it. The quark saturation density depends strongly on the nucleon size parameter. Nuclear interactions shift the high-density equation of state and sound speed. Saturation also sets in earlier than in the noninteracting model.
arxiv-2603-20139: Rai, Facchi, and Tamma estimate all four parameters of a two-channel optical network at Heisenberg scaling. Their scheme is fully Gaussian and feasible with current lab tools. A two-mode squeezed probe enters the network, and balanced homodyne detectors read both outputs. They derive the full classical Fisher information matrix in closed form. All four parameters reach Heisenberg-level sensitivity at once, not one by one. Maximum-likelihood fitting saturates the Cramér-Rao bounds with few repetitions. Low photon numbers suffice, which suits integrated photonics and distributed sensing.
arxiv-2603-20539: Scholes examines quantum-like states in composite systems built from classical parts. Such states can closely mimic separable states of true quantum systems. Scholes shows that quantum-like graphs emulate coupled two-level systems well. The emulated states are separable linear combinations, as in quantum theory. Physical carriers are suggested among classical systems. Candidates include multipole wave moments and networks of phase oscillators. These states could appear in complex networks tied to quantum biology. They might also be engineered into circuits or soft matter.
arxiv-2603-20639: Evans and co-authors argue that the next leap in AI will be social, not a single vast mind. Evolution, they note, made intelligence plural and shared. New agent systems seem to reason by staging inner debates. These inner societies argue, check, and settle hard tasks. Human AI teams also act as hybrid agents no one person controls. They urge a shift from one to one alignment toward rules like those of markets. The result would sprawl like a city of minds.
arxiv-2603-20739: Jiang and co-authors build a Mamba based framework for point cloud tasks across domains. Single task tools often drop in skill when the domain shifts. Transformers cost too much, while plain Mamba orderings drift with viewpoint change. Their design builds sequences from centroid topology and curvature cues. A layered module then steadies reasoning across domains. At test time, a spectral step shifts target features toward source prototypes. They also add MP3DObject, a real scan dataset for tests.
arxiv-2603-20939: Hao and co-authors give chat agents a lasting model of each user's preferences. Most assistants keep no user model, so people must restate their tastes each session. Their VARS framework stores long term and short term vectors for each user in a shared preference space. These vectors bias retrieval from a structured preference memory. Weak feedback scores update the vectors online, with no per user fine tuning. On a multi session benchmark, the agent cuts timeouts and user effort, and its vectors align with real preference overlap.
arxiv-2603-21139: Iddir and co-authors personalize search over XML documents with an ontology and user profiles. Standard search returns the same results to everyone for one query, and ignores user knowledge and goals. Their system represents documents, queries, and profiles as vectors of weighted concepts. The ontology gives more weight to specific, low level concepts, since these carry sharper meaning. Semantic similarity then matches profiles, queries, and documents beyond keywords. Experiments show higher precision and recall than keyword based search.
arxiv-2603-21239: Nguyen and Tân generalize U-unitary Cayley graphs to finite non-commutative rings. These graphs link algebra, number theory, matrix theory, and representation theory. In earlier work on commutative rings, their spectra were described through supercharacter theory. That description yielded classes of gcd-graphs with perfect state transfer. Here the focus shifts to matrix rings over finite fields. They prove that gcd-graphs over these matrix rings have no perfect state transfer. Structural results on connectedness and related traits carry into the new setting.
arxiv-2603-21439: Wang and co-authors tackle a workflow problem in multidisciplinary software development. Domain experts and developers work in mismatched formalisms, so handoffs stay slow and error-prone even with AI coding assistants. Their fix swaps manual coordination for language-model services, step by step, inside a graph-based workflow. They test it on a Volvo Group vehicle API system with 192 endpoints and 776 CAN signals. The workflow hit 93.7 percent F1 and cut per-API time from about five hours to under seven minutes.
arxiv-2603-21839: Mendrot and co-authors solve a generalized Coulomb problem for a spin one-half fermion under the Dirac equation. Scalar, vector, and tensor interactions act as central Coulomb potentials on one plane. A constant term in the tensor coupling creates an effective Coulomb pull, which allows bound states even for pure tensor coupling. Exact bound-state wave functions come out in generalized Laguerre polynomials. The quantization condition gives the exact energy spectrum. A mapping links the planar problem to the spherical one, and known special cases are recovered.
arxiv-2603-21939: Tu and co-authors build FeatDistill, a detector for AI-generated images built for messy real-world conditions. The system runs four Vision Transformer experts, drawn from CLIP and SigLIP lines, so their forensic cues complement. Training data was widened, and a degradation model mimics the quality drops seen online. A second stage distills features inside the model to align representations. Final calls average the four experts' probabilities. Built for the NTIRE challenge, it stayed strong on unseen generators while using about 10 GB of GPU memory.
arxiv-2603-22139: Vo and co-authors compute how ethylene carbonate binds and breaks down on a lithium surface. They find adsorption energies for two binding motifs. They also find the barrier for a ring-opening decomposition step. The team corrects results from clusters of 40 to 100 atoms toward the thermodynamic limit. That lets them use high-level methods like coupled-cluster theory. The high-level results agree within 2 to 5 kcal/mol. Tests show PBE is too inaccurate for barriers, while ωB97X-V looks promising.
arxiv-2603-22239: Chen and co-authors use JWST imaging to map how galaxy size scales with stellar mass. They study star-forming galaxies from redshift 0.5 to 6. The size-mass relation bends at every redshift they probe. The bend sits near ten to the tenth solar masses. Above that mass, the slope flattens and compact galaxies grow common. Quiescent galaxies show a pivot mass that rises with redshift. The authors read the bend as two growth modes. Below the pivot, size tracks halo growth. Above it, galaxies decouple and compact.
arxiv-2603-22339: Czech and co-authors find bias in a popular scaling law method, Chinchilla Approach 2. The method fits parabolas to IsoFLOP curves to pick compute-optimal model sizes. The authors show the parabola fit skews those picks, even on clean synthetic data. On Llama 3 data, the skew wastes about 6.5 percent of the training budget. Three error sources are traced: grid width, off-center sampling, and loss surface asymmetry. Approach 3 avoids most of the bias but has a hard reputation. The authors show those worries are unfounded or fixable.
arxiv-2603-22739: Oellerich and Yamada propose a geometric framework for multi-objective topology optimization. They treat the level set function as a coordinate of a fictitious material. Hamilton's principle then yields a damped wave equation that drives the search. Goals are merged with a weighted sum. The authors show the stationary solutions form a structured set in objective space. The Pareto frontier sits inside it, with weights as intrinsic coordinates. Letting the weights evolve gives a coupled system that explores the goal space. Results show a stable, even cover of the frontier.
arxiv-2603-22939: Beckmann and Risse present FixationFormer, a transformer that uses expert gaze paths to classify chest X-rays. Eye movements hold rich diagnostic knowledge, but they are noisy and sparse in space. Most models flatten gaze into heatmaps, losing the time order. FixationFormer turns gaze paths into token sequences instead. Image and gaze tokens meet through cross-attention. Tests on three public chest X-ray datasets reach state-of-the-art accuracy. The work shows gaze sequences can guide medical image models directly.
arxiv-2603-23339: Kuznetsov and three co-authors present a fast way to predict the point spread function in adaptive optics images. Sharp astronomy analysis needs that blur shape, yet it shifts with wavelength, field spot, and weather. Classic reconstruction needs full optics telemetry and heavy infrastructure. Their Fourier-based model takes a few archive parameters as input. A small neural network then corrects those inputs to match real sky data. On MUSE-NFM stars, median errors stay near 13.5% in Strehl ratio. In crowded omega Centauri fields, errors drop below 5%.
arxiv-2603-23439: Truong and eight co-authors release SIGMA, a physics-based dataset for spotting gas chimneys in seismic images. Gas chimneys mark fluid paths below ground and matter for drilling safety. Strong scattering makes them hard to detect, and labeled data is scarce. SIGMA gives pixel-level chimney masks for detection tasks. It pairs degraded images with clean ground truth for enhancement work. The samples span many geology and survey setups, built with physics-based methods. Benchmark tests show SIGMA is a hard test that aids seismic reading.
arxiv-2603-23539: Gokden argues that some language models reason because they sit at self-organized criticality. PLDR models trained at that edge show outputs like a phase transition. At criticality, the correlation length diverges and outputs settle into a steady state. In that state, outputs act like scaling functions and universality classes. That likeness, he says, is what yields reasoning skill. He defines an order parameter from the outputs' stats. Models reason best when that parameter sits near zero at criticality. Benchmark scores for near-critical training back the claim.
arxiv-2603-23639: Heyen and Sedlmair design augmented reality aids for learning musical instruments. Their first study targets drum kits with plain, glanceable signs shown by a projector. The second turns to guitar, shown as an augmented mirror or through a see-through headset. Those routes allow notes around the instrument and in 3D space. Case study tests show the designs work in practice. The trials also expose design flaws and tech limits worth fixing.
arxiv-2603-23739: Majaess and co-authors re-check whether the benzonitrile cation can be detected in diffuse interstellar gas. They weigh several lines of evidence together. Weak energy sharing inside the molecule favors breakup. Fluorescence is unlikely to save it from breaking apart. Steady photon hits add more damage. Observed diffuse bands also fail to match lab results for this ion. They conclude the ion is largely absent, and they use the case to test broader astrochemistry ideas against new lab spectra and computations.
arxiv-2603-23839: Takata and co-authors simulate a dense gas relaxing between two plates at the same temperature. They use the Enskog equation to test whether free energy falls steadily over time. They compare the original Enskog factor with a modified factor from recent work. With the modified factor, free energy decreases monotonically in their runs. With the original factor, it does not always do so. The two versions also differ in other quantities, most clearly in the density profile over time.
arxiv-2603-24639: Allard and co-authors introduce Experiential Reflective Learning, a self-improvement framework for agents. Agents often ignore past interactions and start each task from scratch, which hurts adaptation. Their method reflects on task outcomes to extract heuristics, short lessons that transfer across tasks. At test time, heuristics are retrieved and placed in the agent's context. On the Gaia2 benchmark, the method lifts success rate by 7.8 percent over a ReAct baseline. Ablations show selective retrieval is key, and heuristics transfer better than raw examples.
arxiv-2603-24739: Sargent and co-authors find a striking excess of red quasars with steep radio spectral slopes. They select quasars from SDSS and use archival radio data to classify the morphologies of 573 red quasars against 1,278 blue ones. Compact red quasars show far more steep-slope emission across three radio bands than any control group. The excess grows with dust extinction, as does the radio detection rate. The authors argue the signal comes from shocks where quasar winds or jets strike the dusty host environment, marking a dusty blow-out phase.
arxiv-2603-24939: Alvarado and co-authors compute log corrections to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. They work with five-dimensional, asymptotically anti-de Sitter charged black holes. The one-loop partition function gathers tensor, vector, and gauge fluctuations around the near-horizon. A generalised Lichnerowicz operator sets the spectrum, deformed by the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. At low temperature, the corrections take a log form set by sector and coupling. Zero modes and their splitting control the result.
arxiv-2603-25039: Bennink and co-authors review how uncertainty methods can guide quantum computing. The review speaks to math and computing readers who are new to the field. It frames quantum work as statistical inference, since noise and chance shape every result. Tools like probability models, Bayesian updates, and sensitivity checks map well onto error spread and device trust. The authors link these tools to live goals like error-aware algorithms at scale and tracking linked errors. The aim is a shared language for judging and fixing today's quantum machines.
arxiv-2603-25239: Yin maps where self-copying patterns can arise in cellular automata. He tests all 262,144 outer-totalistic binary rules with Moore neighborhoods. Only about 7.7 percent let patterns multiply. They cluster at low rule density and low-to-mid background stability, near a weakly chaotic edge. Copying rules also keep total mass closer to steady than others do. A stricter three-step check puts true causal self-replication near 1.6 percent. Bigger neighborhoods raise the rate. Stability and near mass balance mark the border of the living zone.
arxiv-2603-25539: Wang and co-authors recover how jointed objects move by watching hands use them in daily life videos. Drawers and cupboards reveal their hinges through touch, not labels. PAWS mines large sets of first-person video for those interactions. It pulls out the motion and structure of each jointed item at scale. On HD-EPIC and Arti4D it beats prior methods by a clear margin. The harvested joints also help train 3D predictors and guide robot hands. No costly 3D annotation is needed.
arxiv-2603-25839: Marty and co-authors explain the simplicity bias of neural networks through compression. Networks tend to pick simple functions over complex ones. The authors frame supervised learning as two-part lossless compression, in the spirit of minimum description length. A feature is worth learning only when its data savings beat its model cost. This predicts shifts from spurious shortcuts to richer features as data grows. It also predicts cases where less data helps, by blocking unreliable complex cues. A semi-synthetic test matches the predicted path.
arxiv-2603-26139: Deng, Barrière, and Pit-Claudel pin down the complexity of JavaScript regex matching. Modern regex features had left the true cost of matching unclear. Earlier work showed an idealized language with backreferences was PSPACE-complete. The authors prove the same for real JavaScript regex with expanded lower-bounded quantifiers. Hardness survives even without negative lookarounds. Removing all lookarounds yields an OptP-complete parsing problem instead. The core proofs are machine-checked in the Rocq prover.
arxiv-2603-26539: Michaelov and co-authors ask how open a language model must be for science built on it to stay reliable. They sort the ways hidden details of a model's build and deployment can threaten inference. Closed models, they argue, are mostly ill-suited to research, with a few clear exceptions. For each threat they discuss fixes or ways to soften the risk. They urge researchers to name threats and mitigations up front, and to justify why a given model was chosen for a study.
arxiv-2603-26739: Mannucci revisits quantum fuzzy sets, an idea he first proposed in 2006, and extends it in two directions. The original scheme let quantum register states act as membership functions for fuzzy subsets. Now truth values move from pure states to density matrices, filling the whole Bloch ball. That shift captures semantic decoherence, which surface-only states cannot express. He also defines the Q-Matrix, a global density matrix whose local parts yield single fuzzy sets by partial trace. A category of such sets, with monoidal structure, organises the theory.
arxiv-2603-26839: Rodriguez introduces MazeBench, a set of 110 generated maze images for testing multimodal models. Top systems score high: GPT-5.4 reaches 91 percent and Gemini 3.1 Pro 79 percent. The traces tell a different story, though. Models turn images into text grids, then search step by step in tokens. That brute-force style uses thousands of tokens per maze. Given a correct text grid, one model jumped from 6 to 80 percent. Weak visual extraction, not search, is the core gap.
arxiv-2603-27139: Chopra and co-authors present GRACE, a fine-tuning method that makes vision-language models robust on three fronts at once. Fine-tuning usually trades home accuracy, shifted-data accuracy, and attack robustness against each other. The authors blame two geometric faults: sharp minima and unstable features. GRACE flattens minima with curvature-scaled weight perturbations. A feature alignment loss keeps representations steady across clean, attacked, and shifted inputs. On ImageNet fine-tuning of CLIP, home accuracy rose 10.8 points. Attack accuracy rose 13.5 points while shifted-data accuracy held near baseline.
arxiv-2603-27239: Li proposes continuum free-energy computing: a way to solve problems by letting a physical system relax. Each problem is encoded in a free-energy functional that can be set. The system's own dynamics then settle it toward the solution. The idea builds on nonintrinsic Landau theory. Ion-patterned FeRh is offered as a plausible physical host. In FeRh, setting the local phase bias programs the functional. Motion of antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic interfaces supplies the relaxation. Li also names two task classes, a basic protocol, and the main physical limits.
arxiv-2603-27639: Della Fiore sharpens size limits for a special family of codes. B2 codes keep all pair sums distinct. He studies q-ary and constant-weight versions. Difference distributions carry a Fourier structure he exploits. That structure yields a convex relaxation of the problem. Truncated semidefinite programs then certify upper bounds. For q from nine to thirteen, bounds beat the literature. A new bound also covers constant-weight rates.
arxiv-2603-28339: Yu and six co-authors study robotic benches that move through public space and draw people in. The benches reshape a semi-outdoor plaza on their own, gesturing as they go. Passersby treated them in three shifting ways: as robots worth watching, as furniture that steers crowds, and as plain infrastructure. The team proposes a model for how such furniture can move people between these modes on purpose. The work links urban computing with robotic furniture design.
arxiv-2603-28439: Wembe and three co-authors design a controller that steers farm robots by their tool, not just their center. A weeder or cultivator rides at an offset, and ignoring that offset can crush crops. Their closed-form predictive method models the tool as a rigid offset point, with sideways slip and lever-arm effects included. In field tests with two tools, median tracking error fell by 24 to 56 percent. Peak errors at curve changes dropped by up to 70 percent.
arxiv-2603-28639: Ben-Shahar, Bonechi, and Zabzine reformulate three-dimensional gravity with divergenceless vector frames. The idea is inspired by the double copy for Chern-Simons theory. Their formulation is on-shell equivalent to conventional 3D gravity. It also gives a clear geometric reading of the double-copy construction. They relate the new theory to a Chern-Simons-like action. They propose a higher-dimensional origin for it. They also explore extensions that give rise to AdS3 backgrounds. The work links gravity, gauge theory, and geometry in a compact three-dimensional setting.
arxiv-2603-28739: Liu and co-authors give new theory for when transfer learning helps in linear settings. They study ordinary least squares regression and under-parameterized linear neural networks. For regression, they derive exact formulas for expected generalization error with a bias-variance split. Those formulas give necessary and sufficient conditions for auxiliary tasks to help. They also find globally optimal task weights from solvable programs. For neural networks, they derive a non-asymptotic error bound. It gives the first non-vacuous sufficient condition for helpful auxiliary learning in that setting.
arxiv-2603-28839: Crampé and co-authors study Racah type functions and polynomials in one unified algebra frame. They use the meta Racah algebra and its finite representations. The functions appear as overlap coefficients. These link solutions of two eigenvalue problems, one general and one standard, on the same space. From that setup, the team derives their orthogonality relations. They also derive the bispectral traits of the functions. The frame ties finite families of biorthogonal rational functions to Racah polynomials. It gives one route to facts that are often proved case by case.
arxiv-2603-29139: Ai and co-authors introduce SciVisAgentBench, a benchmark for scientific visualization agents. These agents turn plain-language requests into data analysis and visualization tasks. The benchmark holds 108 expert-crafted cases. Cases span domains, data types, complexity levels, and visualization operations. Scoring mixes language-model judging with deterministic checks on images and code. Twelve experts took part in a validity study of the judging. The team also ran early baselines to expose capability gaps.
arxiv-2603-29239: Thawatdamrongkit and co-authors ask whether a diffusion model can picture its own average of a concept. Older averaging methods blur when applied to model samples. Their method, Diffusion Mental Averages, works inside the model's semantic space. It aligns several noise trajectories toward shared coarse-to-fine meaning. The result is one sharp, realistic prototype image. For multimodal concepts, they cluster samples in CLIP space first. Textual inversion or LoRA then bridges clusters back into diffusion space.
arxiv-2603-29339: Xin and co-authors present LongCat-AudioDiT, a diffusion model that turns text into speech. Most systems pass through mel-spectrograms on the way. Their model works directly in waveform latent space instead. That choice cuts compounding errors and simplifies the pipeline. Only a waveform autoencoder and a diffusion backbone are needed. The team also fixes a training-inference mismatch. Adaptive projection guidance replaces the usual guidance method. On the Seed benchmark, their largest model beat the prior best at voice cloning.
arxiv-2603-29439: He and co-authors present PAEMS, an error model for superconducting quantum processors. Error correction decoders need large datasets that hardware cannot supply. Simple noise models lack accuracy, and exact methods grow too fast. PAEMS splits errors qubit by qubit and tracks leakage spread. It learns true qubit errors from repetition-code data. Tests ran on IBM quantum processors. Error correlations fell sharply against prior models, the authors report. It also beat Google's SI1000 model by 58 to 73 percent in accuracy.
arxiv-2603-29539: Karapetyan and co-authors extend agreement trees to repeated measures in clinic studies. Bland-Altman analysis compares two ways of measuring the same subjects. It assumes the two agree the same for all patients. Their trees let agreement shift with patient traits. The mean and spread of gaps between methods split into subject-level parts. That split covers paired and unpaired repeat designs. Simulations held error rates at the set level. A heart output device study showed traits can move agreement.
arxiv-2603-29639: Arreola and Gelaki classify quotients of the Drinfeld double of a finite group scheme. They sort Hopf algebra quotient pairs by group scheme data. Each quotient turns out to be a Hopf algebra extension built from two normal subgroup schemes. The two subgroups centralize each other, and a linking map joins them. A matching surjective map from the double is described. With that in hand, they map the tensor subcategories of the representation category. They find their centers and when they are symmetric. Simple and projective objects are also described.
arxiv-2603-30039: Jones and Malavolta nudge a famous constant's lower bound upward. The Grothendieck constant links functional analysis, quantum information, and optimization. Its exact value remains unknown after decades of work. Davie and Reeds set the best lower bound in the 1980s. The authors prove that bound is not optimal. Their result adds at least ten to the minus twelfth power. Near-extremizers carry real weight on degree-three Hermite terms. A small cubic perturbation then widens the integrality gap.
arxiv-2604-00139: McBride reads the observer proposal in semiclassical gravity through a postmodern lens, treating observer rules as signs of metanarrative breakdown. Recent work leans on such an observer to give closed-universe backgrounds a nontrivial Hilbert space, yet it both supplies and undercuts that perturbative space. Rather than resolving the clash, he argues for accepting the mismatch between accounts with and without an observer as a feature of quantum gravity. He presents this as the first mention of post-postmodernism alongside physics.
arxiv-2604-00339: Yagiz Ihlamur engineers 28 features from founder JSON fields — jobs, education, exits — plus a rule layer and XGBoost boosted stumps. The model reaches F0.5 near 0.30, beating the zero-shot baseline by about 18 points. Adding 9 prose features via Claude Haiku captures about 26 percent of importance but adds no validation signal, since the anonymized prose merely repeats those JSON fields. The ceiling near a quarter there reflects the dataset's information, not a modeling limit, making it a diagnostic for what richer data must include.
arxiv-2604-00639: Hu and colleagues show nonlinear Thouless pumping of gap solitons in quasiperiodic lattices. Such pumping is known in periodic cases, but the quasiperiodic case stayed open. Local potentials rebuild the lattice potential, and a new topological structure from that rebuild governs their motion. That lets them slowly occupy a single band, giving quasi-quantised Thouless pumping. Built-in lattice shakes break that band hold and push them into a drifting regime, yet even there, transport stays limited by a critical rational approximant.
arxiv-2604-00739: Hashim, Soboczenski, and Cairns extend the COMPASS transformer model into BioCOMPASS for predicting how patients respond to immunotherapy. Rather than feeding biomarkers in as inputs, they add loss terms that line those signals up with the model's middle layers. Treatment gating and a pathway consistency loss complete the design. Tested by holding out whole cohorts, cancer types, and treatments in turn, the added parts improved generalization to unseen patient groups.
arxiv-2604-01639: Han and colleagues evaluate three open-weight models on 677 GSM8K problems. All three models exhibit large answer-flip rates from 28.8 percent to 45.1 percent, with number paraphrasing more disruptive than name swaps. Activation patching reveals a design divide: Llama-3 failures are recoverable by patching at set layers, while Mistral and Qwen failures are broadly distributed. They propose a failure taxonomy of localized, distributed, and entangled failures: steering vectors and layer fine-tuning recover a larger share of localized failures than of entangled or distributed ones.
arxiv-2604-01939: Baaj and Marquis compute Kullback Leibler projections from possibilistic data for classification. Each instance carries a plausibility distribution over classes. From it they build a convex admissible set from possibility, necessity and shape constraints. Those constraints: equal degrees share chances, larger degrees get larger ones. Given a probability vector, they compute its closest projection onto that set. Training minimizes that gap with Dykstra's algorithm and Bregman projections. Made-up and ChaosNLI tests show it is efficient and can improve performance.
arxiv-2604-02239: Banerjee, Bringmann and El Bachraoui settle two conjectures of Andrews and Bachraoui on congruences for restricted two color partitions. The conjectures claimed Ramanujan type congruences and a vanishing identity for a limiting sequence. By tying the generating function to modular forms and mock theta functions, the authors prove both claims. The argument closes the conjectures with tools from modular forms and mock theta functions.
arxiv-2604-02339: Asawa, Dimakis and Zaharia teach language models from natural language context with as few as three query examples. Their SIEVE pipeline splits context into parts, pairs synthetic queries with only the relevant parts to make higher quality rollouts, then distills context into model weights. In reasoning settings where context is essential, including custom domains, RuleArena and a one book translation task, SIEVE beats prior context distillation methods using just three examples. The work shows parametric learning need not be data hungry.
arxiv-2604-02439: Mallick and three colleagues define the absolute Schmidt number, a property of quantum states whose entanglement dimension cannot be raised by any global unitary change. They characterize the states that keep this number fixed under all such changes, then build witness-based and moment-based tests to spot states that lack the property. They also add two resource measures for such states and extend the idea to quantum channels.
arxiv-2604-03239: Tsiokos builds a testable account of agency inside Six Birds Theory, which treats large objects as induced closures rather than primitives. An agent becomes a maintained theory object whose feasible policies can steer outside futures while staying viable, checked through ledger-gated feasibility, viability kernels, empowerment, and packaging maps. Ring-world experiments separate agenthood from mere agency without invoking goals or consciousness.
arxiv-2604-03439: Luo and colleagues build a machine-learning heat flux closure for inertial confinement fusion plasmas that works on coarse and fine grids alike. Trained on particle-in-cell runs with a Fourier neural operator, the closure matches heat trends when placed in the electron energy model. Models trained on coarse data still predict heat flux well on much finer ones, bridging kinetic and fluid views.
arxiv-2604-03539: Zhang and colleagues introduce CB-Ver, a framework for checking long-run stable traits of network control planes, such as reach, access control, and path length. The key idea is a CB-graph. When users supply specs for each part, CB-Ver checks part requirements at once with an SMT solver and builds the graph. If the graph connects all nodes, the specs are valid, more long-run stable traits can be checked, and fault tolerance can be judged.
arxiv-2604-03639: Ander Arriola Corpion and Cecília Salgado studied families of genus-2 curves lying on a K3 surface over a number field. They showed that after passing to a suitable finite extension, infinitely many fibers have Jacobians whose Mordell-Weil rank jumps above the usual value. They also gave geometric conditions under which such jumps occur on a large, non-thin set of fibers.
arxiv-2604-03839: Meilun Zhou and Alina Zare argued that object detectors trained only on task loss learn shortcuts that miss the structure of their annotations. Their framework injects annotation-guided embeddings into the detector backbone, building dense feature grids that steer region proposals and detection heads. Across wildlife and remote sensing sets, the approach sharpened object focus, cut background sensitivity, and generalized better to unseen or weakly supervised tasks.
arxiv-2604-03939: Chi-Shian Dai and Jun Shao fused outside machine-learning guesses into multinomial logistic regression for a primary study. Outside guesses supply rich moment rules through a data-based method, robust to covariate shift under mild overlap without density-ratio modeling. The method handles rough results, partial inputs, input shift, and concept shift in outside sources. Theory gives soundness, normal shape in large samples, and strict gains under mild rules, with tests and a food-survey use.
arxiv-2604-04139: Vikram Kamath Cannanure and team piloted a WhatsApp chatbot with language-model content for teacher training in Cameroon, against an online-form baseline. In a mixed-methods study with 47 primary school teachers, the chatbot scored higher on perceived usability and overall experience, while learnability stayed comparable. Gains came from platform familiarity, low interaction overhead, and modular content, but were limited by connectivity, prepaid data costs, and English-French language needs. The authors sketch next steps for multilingual, culturally grounded interaction and prompting support.
arxiv-2604-04239: Sajad Ghawami audited whether multimodal cancer survival models give calibrated probabilities, not just strong rankings. Yet across 290 fold-level tests, 166 rejected correct calibration at the median event time after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. In one experiment, all three models failed 1-calibration on most folds, and MCAT's C-index hit 0.817 on GBMLGG yet it failed all five folds. Gating fusion tracked calibration better than bilinear or concatenation fusion, and Platt scaling cut miscalibration without harming discrimination.
arxiv-2604-04539: Kim and colleagues present FlashSAC, a fast off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm built on Soft Actor-Critic for robot control. Off-policy methods learn from broader distributions but converge slowly and unstably, as many updates let critic errors accumulate. FlashSAC sharply cuts gradient updates while compensating with larger models and higher data throughput, bounding weight, feature and gradient norms to curb critic errors. Across over 60 tasks in 10 simulators, it beats Proximal Policy Optimization and off-policy baselines in final performance and training efficiency, with largest gains on dexterous manipulation.
arxiv-2604-05239: Li and Schwalbe-Koda show that a measure of information entropy in systems serves as a shared variable for rare event sampling across atom and condensed systems. It biases runs toward entropy-changing shapes via tuned sampling, weighing novelty and heat access. Blind search enables finding stable basins and reaction pathways, including rival channels closed to usual order rules. It is shown across five systems spanning shape sampling, even seeding, glass growth, and solid-state phase shifts.
arxiv-2604-05539: Haufe and Stolzenburg check offer papers for rule-bound public bodies with a neurosymbolic pipeline. A language model pulls out facts, then a Logic Tensor Network blends them into a choice that can be audited via predicate scores, rule scores, and cited text. On a real corpus it matches rival models on scores while adding clear, modular, explainable checks.
arxiv-2604-05739: Lim builds Iwasawa theory for abelian varieties with potentially good ordinary reduction at primes above p. The results feed Diophantine stability and integrally Diophantine cases, sharpening Mazur growth conjecture work by earlier authors with tighter bounds. Finally, the study extends to elliptic curves of good supersingular type at p, with a matching analysis that tracks the same questions in full detail.
arxiv-2604-06139: McGlynn and Hebborn model carbon-22 as a carbon-20 core plus two halo neutrons, putting numbers on the uncertainty for the first time. They treat the core-neutron interaction with a Bayesian approach and carry its uncertainty through to bound and scattering states and to dipole strength. Comparing predicted matter radius with measured values suggests carbon-22 binds by less than 0.35 megaelectronvolts, with most of the nucleus in an s-wave squared configuration. Their dipole analysis finds final-state interaction essential, with strength uncertainties near 50 percent driven mainly by ground-state uncertainty.
arxiv-2604-06239: Shvets proves that the ratio of an Apéry-like sequence to the Domb numbers converges to seven twenty-fourths of zeta of 3. A related infinite sum equals fifty-six thirds of zeta of 3. As a corollary, he establishes the value twelve over seven zeta of 3 conjectured by the Ramanujan Machine project for Z_2. Eichler integrals of weight-4 modular forms, Atkin-Lehner involutions, and level-6 eta products drive the proof.
arxiv-2604-06839: Hosamani finds the Mostar index extremes for graphs with given cut edges. The Mostar index sums over edges the gap between vertex counts nearer each end. For connected graphs of order n with k cut edges, the maximum follows a formula in k and n. It is attained by a complete graph on n minus k vertices with k pendant edges on one vertex. A lower bound and its extremal graphs follow. Results extend to graphs with a cyclomatic number plus cut edges, completing the picture.
arxiv-2604-06939: Chen and four colleagues steady long-form video with Grounded Forcing. Step-by-step video tools promise endless video but suffer fading meaning, drifting visuals, and slipping control. Tools treat each flaw alone, capping coherence. Grounded Forcing ties video making to stable meaning cores. A dual memory cache splits local motion and global meaning anchors. A dual-anchor tweak keeps position codes in range and global meaning time-free. A one-sided recache smooths meaning handover across prompt changes. Tests show much better long-range hold and steady visuals.
arxiv-2604-07539: Leverett and van der Ham-de Vos prove a single C program admits infinitely many distinct CVE-listed software flaws. Their Vulnerability Factory case uses basic set theory and MITRE CVE counting rules. A model-checking sketch backs endless flaw making, and a Turing-machine account places the result in computer theory. The paper coins flaw abundance, the spread of flaw classes across the global software corpus. It splits infinite flaws from exploits, with fewer than 6 percent of CVEs ever used.
arxiv-2604-07739: Jiao and nine colleagues ask how recommendation systems can keep adapting as user behavior drifts without retraining on everything they collect. They test ways of picking small, informative slices of interaction data and find that gradient-based representations paired with distribution matching lift later performance while holding up under drift. The upshot is practical: careful data curation makes frequent model updates cheaper and scalable in live systems.
arxiv-2604-07839: Sabbineni and four colleagues propose UDSS, a hardware-anchored middleware for sharing personal data across smart TVs, consoles, set-top boxes, and similar devices. Onboarding today means tedious manual entry and opaque sharing rules across a fragmented device landscape. The platform-agnostic framework enables privacy-first exchange between device platforms and third-party apps. A contextual scope enforcement mechanism limits exposure by user intent, treating sign-in and sign-up differently. Unlike cloud-anchored identity standards, the design roots trust in device hardware rather than remote servers.
arxiv-2604-07939: Malvezzi and four colleagues present RAGE-XY, a real-time estimator of forces and motion for autonomous race cars using only standard onboard sensors. Building on the earlier RAGE system, it infers vehicle speed, tire slip angles, and forces from inertial sensors and radar. An online radar calibration step sharpens lateral speed estimates despite misalignment. The vehicle model also grows from a single-track approximation to a tricycle model, adding rear lengthwise tire forces to lateral dynamics. High-fidelity tests on the EAV-24 car show better accuracy and robustness.
arxiv-2604-08039: Zaigrajew and four colleagues introduce LINE, a training-free iterative method for labeling single neurons in vision models with open vocabularies. Interpreting single neurons matters for grasping decisions and ensuring AI safety. Existing methods restrict search to preset vocabularies or produce overly specific descriptions that miss global concepts. Operating strictly black-box, LINE uses a large language model plus a text-to-image generator to propose and refine concepts in a loop guided by activation history. It reaches leading results across architectures, with AUC gains up to 0.11 on ImageNet.
arxiv-2604-08139: Ivanovskikh and eight colleagues describe quantum wave mixing in a linked waveguide-QED pair of super-cold qubits. The probe gets an outside coherent tone plus light from a driven source qubit. From the source glow's field link functions, they build an effective master-equation model for the probe, finding where incident fluorescence shows anomalous correlations. When the Rayleigh part of the source spectrum is suppressed, probe equations match those of a qubit under a plain tone plus broadband squeezed light. The source light itself is non-Gaussian.
arxiv-2604-08239: Bianchin and 14 colleagues present extended coronal emission and clues to a possible dual AGN in the merger J1356+1026. The local obscured quasar J1356+1026, at redshift 0.1232, has North and South nuclei, but despite numerous efforts, the South one was unconfirmed as an AGN. MIRI/MRS on JWST yields new evidence that the South nucleus may indeed host an AGN with log bolometric luminosity 43.4. Support comes from strong coronal emission there and a spectral shape differing from the North nucleus and narrow-line region.
arxiv-2604-08539: Hu and five colleagues train OpenVLThinkerV2, a generalist multimodal reasoning model, with a new Gaussian GRPO objective that forces each task's advantage spread toward a standard normal shape. That leveling keeps gradients fair across tasks with wildly varied rewards and guards against heavy tail outliers. Added length and entropy shaping balance perception with reasoning, and the model leads strong open and proprietary rivals across 18 benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-08639: Ray and Srivastava benchmark ten uncertainty quantification methods for deep learning against a stripped down variant of their VOLTA system. It keeps just a deep encoder, trainable prototypes, cross entropy loss, and post hoc temperature scaling. Across image, corruption, noise, and tabular tests, VOLTA matches or beats most baselines. Accuracy reaches 0.864 on CIFAR-10, with far lower calibration error and strong out of distribution detection. Adaptive temperature and deep encoders prove key in ablations.
arxiv-2604-08739: Caliskan and three colleagues present RansomTrack, a hybrid framework for catching ransomware before encryption ends. Static features come from the Radare2 sandbox, while dynamic signals like memory protection changes, mutex creation, registry access, and network activity come from the Frida toolkit. Their public dataset spans 165 ransomware and benign families, and ensemble models reach up to 96 percent accuracy with ROC-AUC 0.99, checking each sample in about 9 seconds.
arxiv-2604-08939: Zhou and four colleagues ask why powerful optimizers weaken multi-task learning, in which one model learns several jobs together. They show that gradients taken at each moment play only a small part in the parameter updates, so schemes meant to resolve clashes between tasks fall short. They also observe that the Muon optimizer already behaves like a multi-task learner. Their APT framework pairs adaptive momentum with a light method that preserves direction for Muon, and trials on four task sets lift existing approaches.
arxiv-2604-09139: Banerjee and seven colleagues measure the extragalactic background light, the faint glow from all stars, galaxies, and feeding black holes across the visible universe. Using 15 years of Fermi telescope data from 1576 blazars, they trace how gamma rays are dimmed by that glow across 19 redshift bins out to redshift 4.3. The dimming signal stands out at about 23 sigma, and the rebuilt glow history broadly matches recent models. The authors call this the sharpest such measurement yet made with GeV gamma rays.
arxiv-2604-09239: Ashurov and Shamuratov investigate the backward problem for a multi-term time-fractional diffusion equation. Such problems are ill-posed: a small change in final data can cause large changes in the initial state. The authors show that with sufficiently smooth current data, a solution exists, is unique, and is stable. A key difficulty is the multinomial Mittag-Leffler function in the denominator, whose asymptotic behavior they characterize from recent work. They also prove conditional stability under a prior bound, plus a best smoothing property.
arxiv-2604-09539: Santos-Santos, Frenk, and Navarro combine a top-resolution simulation of a Milky Way-mass halo with the GALFORM galaxy model. Their model caps the total ever accreted at a few hundred. It matches the massive end of the observed satellite mass function. It predicts many ultra-faint dwarfs fainter than absolute magnitude minus 5 are still missing. The missing dwarfs should shun the inner galaxy and resemble new ultra-faint compact satellites. Their survival points to cuspy dark-matter halos.
arxiv-2604-09639: Bose tackles multi-view 3D stylization usable downstream without camera poses or a 3D representation in training. Stylizing each view alone drifts textures, warps edges, and shades inconsistently, hurting downstream tasks. The proposed feed-forward network trains with per-scene test-time optimization, coupling appearance transfer with geometry preservation. An AdaIN-inspired loss from a frozen VGG-19 encoder matches moments to a style image. Correspondence and depth losses stabilize structure across viewpoints. Tests on Tanks and Temples and Mip-NeRF 360 show reduced distortion and stronger trajectory and point-cloud consistency.
arxiv-2604-09739: Fazlollahi extends the thermodynamic account of gravity in the Jacobson method by stretching the Clausius relation with a complex entropy rule. Entropy shifts appear as changes of the gravitational coupling, spanning modified gravity theories, though usual entropy fixes cannot remove space-time breakdowns. An entropy form using quantum traits at horizon degrees of freedom changes the picture. The early cosmos gains a smooth phase with finite Hubble rate, yielding de Sitter-like rapid growth, finite entropy, and heat. At late times, the theory matches the workings of loop quantum cosmology.
arxiv-2604-09839: Mishra, Khashabi, and Liu frame activation steering as a surjectivity question: with one model fixed, can each steered activation be traced back through the model's natural forward pass? On practical assumptions, they prove that steering drives the residual stream away from states that discrete prompts can reach. Almost surely, no prompt recreates the same inner behavior that steering produces. The team illustrates this finding empirically across three widely used language models. The findings draw a formal line between prompt-based control and white-box steering.
arxiv-2604-10139: Chen, Grossi, and Li study positive solutions of a semilinear elliptic Robin problem as the Robin parameter tends to zero. For every exponent value, the solution behaves like a constant in the limit. The constant itself, however, depends strongly on the exponent. Below 1, solutions blow up uniformly; at 1, the eigenvalue case, they converge to a constant; above 1, they converge uniformly to zero. In critical and supercritical regimes, existence is no longer guaranteed in advance. For a ball domain with the parameter below a stated threshold, a radial positive solution exists.
arxiv-2604-10539: Mao, Wang, Ester, and Li shrink the memory cost of long chat model runs. Key value caches speed replies yet swell with sequence length, choking tight hardware. Old offload tricks pick tokens poorly and fade on long chains of thought. Their IceCache groups kindred tokens into neat blocks under a live ranked store. With a 256 token budget, it keeps 99 percent of full cache accuracy on LongBench.
arxiv-2604-10839: Hernández and Castellanos study a relativistic model for self-bound Bose-Einstein condensates, built on a nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation with cubic and logarithmic terms. The frame catches droplet traits like self-trapping and shapes from rival terms. In the slow limit, they get a Gross-Pitaevskii equation with a logarithmic fix, matching cold gas models past mean-field theory. They build the Lagrangian density, find conserved traits via Noether, and work out the tensor. Number runs lay groundwork for an account of condensates, whose motion shows wave regimes.
arxiv-2604-10939: Cheng and Liu calculate lifetimes and semileptonic decay widths of doubly heavy baryons in heavy quark expansion. They include corrections to dimension-three, dimension-five, and dimension-six operators, plus leading dimension-seven terms. Matrix elements come from a bag model. Lifetime order places Xi_cc++ above Omega_cc+ above Xi_cc+ among doubly charmed baryons. W-exchange drives the large lifetime split in the doubly charmed sector. For Xi_cc+, the leading spectator effect beats the nominally leading term, so its lifetime value stays only indicative.
arxiv-2604-11139: Lygatsika and four colleagues report on the GPU port of Abinit, a code for plane-wave density functional theory calculations. Large atomic structure calculations require computing the wave function by solving Kohn-Sham equations over many plane waves. Porting to GPU nodes relies on vendor libraries and revisions of iterative diagonalization. This finds GPU-efficient operations such as linear algebra and FFTs. The paper discusses Abinit on multi-GPU architectures, giving speed results for mixed CPU-GPU nodes against CPU-only nodes. Special focus goes to testing two solvers.
arxiv-2604-11239: Sigfrid, Fackle-Fornius, and Miller compare ways to shorten the Parkinson's questionnaire used to track motor symptoms. Ranking items by Fisher information beat random choice, coordinate descent did better still, and adaptive selection added a small further gain. For a five-item subset, expected standard deviation fell 14 percent with ranking, 26 percent with coordinate descent, and 34 percent with adaptive selection, though the adaptive figure is a best-case limit.
arxiv-2604-11439: De Simone and nine colleagues map the dusty streamer feeding the M512 protostar in Orion, one of the most massive streamers known. Archival ALMA observations of four molecular tracers reveal chemical layering: C18O on the western side, DCO+ in the middle, and N2D+ farther east. The pattern suggests environmental shaping rather than a single infalling flow, with only the densest gas near the protostar likely to accrete onto the disk. The bulk of the streamer thus carries the imprint of its cloud, complicating streamer-to-disk growth stories.
arxiv-2604-12039: Sossi and Bower examine Earth's origins via shifts in ten element-making isotope quirks across planet and space-rock parents. Space rocks split into carbon-poor, likely inner, and carbon-rich, likely outer, bodies, yet Earth was thought to hold minor or large outer stuff. Stretching a carbon-poor array always meets bulk rocky Earth makeup within one standard spread. Earth therefore formed only from inner stuff of steady makeup, unlike any chondrite, while Mercury and Venus look more extreme, hinting at a spatial or time gradient.
arxiv-2604-12139: Schaller and Boyd estimate the matrix linking log price changes to log demand changes across a product set, from observed prices and integer demand counts. They impose a factor structure, diagonal plus low rank, and compare three fitting methods for the resulting bi-convex likelihood problem. Gradient ascent wins on speed while matching the others, and on synthetic data the likelihood-best settings also maximize profit under optimal pricing.
arxiv-2604-12239: Reddy and Liu estimate distance to nearby vehicles from a single camera by exploiting standardized United States license plate lettering as passive markers. Geometric priors resolve scale ambiguity with no training data or active light. A four-method detector reads plates across lighting, a three-stage engine identifies the issuing state, and hybrid depth fusion with a Kalman filter smooths distance, relative speed, and time to collision. Tests show a 36 percent cut in distance variance versus plate-width methods.
arxiv-2604-12339: Rodríguez and Sengupta build coils for vacuum stellarator fields from equilibrium traits alone, through a current potential on flux surfaces. Level sets of the Boozer toroidal angle serve as proxy coils, and key complexity measures, above all coil non-planarity, prove strongly governed by local magnetic field traits. The approach promises a practical proxy for coil design and deeper insight into equilibrium-coil links.
arxiv-2604-12939: Ao Yang and two colleagues show late signals in non-Hermitian impurity scattering follow poles. In Hermitian scattering, each isolated exponential marks a bound state. That link breaks in non-Hermitian bands. Isolated complex frequencies from Green functions govern the late signal. Poles need not match static bound states; one may appear alone, while a bound state may stay hidden. The rest is background from complex continuum edges. Real-time analytic structure, not static eigenvalues alone, organizes scattering.
arxiv-2604-13139: Liu and 11 colleagues build a cheap self-driving lab for physics teaching, an Internet-of-Things platform that lets students run machine learning experiments hands-on. An Arduino controller, a multi-wavelength LED array, and light sensors generate live optical datasets for training methods from traversal search to Bayesian inference and deep learning. The closed-loop setup automates collection, cleaning, training, and validation, and at about $60 it shows deep learning capturing complex nonlinear relationships best.
arxiv-2604-13839: Cuceu and Bizouard offer Basilic, a pipeline for Bayesian analysis of short gravitational-wave bursts. Built on bilby, it handles model selection and parameter estimation with modular burst models and HTCondor support, so analyses run fast. A case study pits a black hole merger against a cosmic string signal in injection campaigns. Besides the known high-mass shape degeneracy, high anti-aligned spins at moderate mass also mimic strings. The authors propose a data-driven degeneracy study for inconclusive Bayes factors, the likely regime for future low-SNR detections.
arxiv-2604-13939: Amster and Polotto build a multi-stage pipeline to spot Bethesda cells in Pap smear images for a cytology challenge. An ensemble of YOLO and U-Net models first finds candidate cells, then overlap removal and a binary classifier refine the picks. Their system took second place, scoring 0.5909 on mAP50-95, showing how combined detection and cleanup stages lift accuracy on clinical microscopy.
arxiv-2604-14039: Callsen and colleagues model hole and spin motion in an antiferromagnet close to half filling with a conserving diagrammatic method for the Fermi-Hubbard model. Doping creates four hole pockets of magnetic polarons that dampen as doping rises, while the magnon spectrum softens from hole-induced frustration. The method also reproduces the experimental contrast between in-phase and out-of-phase lattice modulations, linked to pseudogap physics.
arxiv-2604-14339: Li and five colleagues propose RoPE-Perturbed Self-Distillation, a regularizer for positional robustness in long-context adaptation. Standard adaptation stays brittle: accuracy hinges on evidence placement, with high positional variance at fixed format and difficulty. The method builds alternate views of each sequence by perturbing RoPE indices, moving context parts to new positions, and trains consistent predictions across views by self-distillation. Tests on Llama-3-8B and Qwen-3-4B show steady gains on benchmarks, including RULER-64K and RULER-256K, plus better length extrapolation beyond the training window.
arxiv-2604-14739: Lettner, El Ashhab, Hagenmeyer, and Schäfer weigh time-series foundation models against task-specific models for day-ahead probabilistic electricity price forecasting in European bidding zones. Foundation models Moirai and ChronosX beat models trained from scratch on CRPS, energy score, and interval calibration across market conditions. Yet a well-tuned NHITS model with quantile-regression averaging came very close, and with richer features or few-shot adaptation from other markets it sometimes won outright. The lesson is practical: weigh computing cost against small performance gains before choosing.
arxiv-2604-14839: Xu and eight colleagues target a neglected gap in multimodal recommendation: items start modality-rich while users start from random vectors, leaving a semantic gap. Their SG-URInit builds each user's starting representation from modality features of touched items plus global cluster features. The result captures both item-level and cluster-level semantics. Training-free and model-agnostic, it slots into existing models with no extra training cost. Experiments on real datasets show clear performance gains, plus relief for item cold-start and faster convergence.
arxiv-2604-15139: Bilgin and colleagues propose ternary noise modulation, a wireless scheme that sends data through noise itself. Where binary noise modulation uses two variance levels, the new scheme adds a third state, deliberate silence. Pairing two consecutive noise blocks yields eight valid state combos, carrying three bits per signaling interval. A two-stage receiver first spots silence by its mean, then sorts low and high variance.
arxiv-2604-15739: Huang, Yang, Liu, and Li prove that k-token next-token guessing in generative recommendation matches full-item-vocab top-likelihood guessing exactly. This needs a one-to-one map from items to k-token strings. The match holds for both chain and side-by-side token splits, the two top shop schemes. The proof gives the first firm theory base for the top shop recipe and steers next tuning work.
arxiv-2604-16039: Ashton and four colleagues present a hierarchical Bayesian model to measure glitch rates in ground gravitational wave detectors. Glitches cut reach and can overlap signals, biasing cosmic readings. The model reaches into the low signal regime without Gaussian noise, if the population is modeled well. It covers short glitches only, via an antiglitch model. Applied to fourth run data, it gives time-tracked rates matching trigger counts without thresholds. Rates convert into a glitch chance, hinting withdrawn candidate GW230630_070659 is likely two glitches.
arxiv-2604-16439: Gu offers a counterexample to a recent conjecture about the adiabatic theorem for quantum quenches within a single phase. The conjecture held that the overlap between the starting ground state and later states would peak for the later ground state. Gu constructs a local, translationally invariant, gapped free-fermion case where this fails. The before and after systems link through a symmetry-preserving gapped path, with a continuous spectrum in the large-system limit. The short note shows the claim does not hold in general.
arxiv-2604-16539: Chillara predicts black-hole growth regimes from broadband photometry alone. Webb finds of little red dots may disfavor light seeds, while heavy-seed masses stay poorly constrained. Rubin LSST will image galaxies without direct black-hole mass measurements. Forward-modelling three simulations into LSST bands, she trains an ensemble classifier. It reaches 91 to 94 percent accuracy on two simulations under LSST limits. Cross-simulation transfer still reaches 83 to 89 percent, driven mainly by host colors. That establishes a validated baseline for post-seeding growth regimes.
arxiv-2604-16739: Kishimoto, Stanley and Valenzuela Ruiz study the homology of the Moment-Angle complex for a triangulated compact orientable manifold. The total rank satisfies a bound with equality exactly when the triangulation is tight. Using Lefschetz duality, the authors build a short exact functor sequence. That sequence gives a new Double Homology duality result for tight manifold shapes.
arxiv-2604-16839: Zhu and colleagues propose HeLa-Mem, a bio memory architecture treating memory as a dynamic Hebbian graph. Fixed context windows cannot keep coherence across long chats, and old systems store history as loose embedding vectors. Three life tricks are central yet largely absent: association, consolidation and spreading firing. An episodic graph evolves through co-firing patterns, while a semantic store fills via Hebbian boiling of densely linked hubs. On LoCoMo, HeLa-Mem beats prior work across four question kinds while using far fewer context tokens.
arxiv-2604-17139: Liu and four colleagues expose a flaw in multi-agent voting. When corrupted agents form a local majority, vote aggregation collapses, blind to flawed intermediate logic. Their Token-Level Round-Robin Collaboration interleaves generation token by token within a shared context, turning aggregation from a brittle count of final votes into an interwoven chain. Theory shows the honest model's pull can overpower adversarial attacks even under a hostile majority, and experiments confirm robust accuracy past that threshold.
arxiv-2604-17339: Forlivesi, Valentini, and Chiani propose a fault-tolerant syndrome-extraction scheme for CSS quantum codes, called the cut-cat state method. Each helper qubit touches two data qubits in a non-fault-tolerant way, but extra cat stabilizer measurements catch and correct the resulting hook errors. The design keeps the parallel interactions of cat-based extraction while more than halving the qubits needed at once. Against leading flag-based protocols, it also cuts two-qubit gate counts as code distance grows.
arxiv-2604-17539: Ilker and three colleagues build a full theory of chemically active emulsions in the hydrodynamic limit. Their framework stays thermodynamically sound while fuel molecules break equilibrium through chemo-stating. For ternary mixes with active reactions, they derive long-scale dynamics where time symmetry breaks, going beyond Active Model B+, the generic theory of active phase separation. A test on a Flory-Huggins model predicts microphases when the effective interfacial energy turns negative, plus a bubbly split once noise enters, and a new dynamic active filament phase.
arxiv-2604-17839: Adlam draws a parallel between famous black-hole paradoxes and extended Wigner's Friend puzzles, asking what the resemblance can teach about quantum measurement. Treating the analogy seriously, Adlam argues, favours readings that make relations intrinsic to physical systems rather than merely effective or emergent. The same comparison also supports accounts that allow a kind of retrocausality, where later events bear on earlier ones.
arxiv-2604-18239: Chen and seven colleagues study preference optimization, the training that aligns language models with human preferences. Margin-based methods often suppress the chosen answer while trying to suppress the rejected one, with no general fix across objectives. A unified incentive-score split shows objectives share local update directions and differ only in scalar weights. From it, the authors derive a disentanglement band condition and a reward-calibration method that rebalances updates, improving downstream results across several settings.
arxiv-2604-18339: Mera and 14 colleagues present MOFAT, a public tool for probing where molecules form in supernovae through infrared bands. The tool fits steady radiative transfer models with clumpy 3D shapes to precise data. Applied to the 2024ggi event at 285 and 385 days after explosion, it shows CO sparking SiO growth inside. SiO mass falls roughly tenfold as its inner edge recedes from 1,500 to 1,000 kilometers per second, with clumping visible but little cooling or dust.
arxiv-2604-18439: Shi, Pan, Ban, and Chen carry shortcuts to adiabaticity from quantum motion into classical dissipative Lagrangian systems. Using a coupled radial-angular arm as a model, they work backward on the Euler-Lagrange equations with Rayleigh friction from endpoint-still paths. Force and torque curves reveal how shape-based coupling grows errors and extra energy. Smooth shortcut plans trade against motor-bounded time-optimal options and PID tracking, with a single mid-course fix easing early drifts.
arxiv-2604-18739: Chen and four colleagues derive Discrete Tilt Matching, a likelihood-free way to fine-tune masked diffusion language models with reinforcement learning. Standard methods rely on sequence likelihoods that are intractable for such models. The new method instead matches local unmasking posteriors at the state level under reward tilting, using a weighted cross-entropy objective with control variates for stability. Tuning LLaDA-8B-Instruct with it yields strong gains on Sudoku and Countdown, staying competitive on MATH500 and GSM8K.
arxiv-2604-19139: Wu and six colleagues review verbal tics in frontier models across eight groups. Repeated praise, canned reassurance, familiar contrasts, and conspicuous vocabulary recur in discussions. They check products against official release and API documentation, with evidence to October 2026. The research documents common patterns and agreement warping judgment, while measurements of releases are sparse. User reports mix complaints with improved writing. The authors propose measures of recurrence, appropriateness, and belief distortion, with records and notes, making quality claims testable as services change.
arxiv-2604-19239: Kreutz and Ziereis study how rigid polycrystals form from atomistic particle systems with general interactions. Atomistic energy is treated as a sum over particles, favoring atoms that sit locally like a reference lattice, with no lattice assumed in advance. The authors prove a discrete-to-continuum limit for setups with finite surface-energy scaling, using gamma-convergence. The resulting continuum theory uses piecewise constant fields for local orientation, and its energy sits on grain boundaries between regions of constant orientation.
arxiv-2604-19339: Wang and colleagues tackle ultra-fine-grained visual categorization, where highly similar subtypes must be told apart from limited training samples. Whole-picture cues like leaf contours in near-twin cultivars are little studied, yet building them usually demands massive data. Their Divide-and-Conquer Holistic Cognition Network breaks whole-picture cues into spatially linked subtle gaps and builds recognition step by step. The split cuts the task down and lessens its need for large training sets.
arxiv-2604-19539: Li and colleagues build a fast method for making visible windows and screening their quality for regional radar reconnaissance. Such work needs windows that are workable in shape under side-looking constraints and yield readable image quality. Building runs in three stages. Coarse angular screening drops orbit arcs with no likely target intersection. A planar curve test fixes precise spans, and edge splitting then fixes entry and exit times within a second.
arxiv-2604-19839: Bang and four colleagues propose EUEA, a framework that fine-tunes vision-language models in four core skills for embodied agents that follow instructions. The skills are object perception for spotting relevant objects and task planning for generating interaction subgoals. Action understanding judges success odds, and goal recognition tells when a goal is complete. Fine-tuned this way, the models handle environmental understanding better, failing less in use and leaning less on metadata during execution.
arxiv-2604-20039: Alderete and three colleagues test whether scaffolding lets LLM agents revise their hypothesis space, not just update beliefs within it. Their two-part design pairs context graphs, typed state machines that structure search, with dynamic behaviors that spot weak hypotheses and expand them at runtime. Across 1,085 trials the parts help differently. Context graphs drive post-switch thinking quality, making up 94 percent of the accuracy gain, while the dynamic part keeps the agent ready to think by catching regime shifts early.
arxiv-2604-20439: Mu and five colleagues test whether the newly observed K(1690) state, a candidate strange crypto-exotic meson reported by COMPASS, can be captured by local meson-meson currents under QCD sum rules. They build a set of independent local color-singlet currents with spin-parity zero minus and work out their sum rules. For currents with reliable Borel windows, the extracted mass scales sit near two gigaelectronvolts, well above the observed mass. None of the chosen currents yields a separate low-lying pole matching the COMPASS signal.
arxiv-2604-20539: Sun and nine colleagues build an animator-centered system for generating skeletons, the joint rigs that drive 3D character motion, for detailed objects. Current deep learning methods struggle with complex modern models and give animators little control. The team curates 82,633 rigged meshes, adds semantic-aware tokenization that groups bones by meaning for auto-regressive modeling, and designs a learnable density interval module for soft, direct control over bone density. Tests show high-quality skeletons on hard inputs, meeting two key requirements from professional animators.
arxiv-2604-21139: Paul Bogdan and Jack Lindsey probe how language models track several entities at once inside one token's activations. Their multi-slot method untangles a token's signal into separate slots for the entity now described and the one just before it. The earlier slot aids relational guesses and clash detection but not direct fact questions, and open models nearly fail when one token must carry two subject-verb-object links, unlike newer frontier models.
arxiv-2604-21239: Takuya Takahashi works out frequency shifts for gravitational waves from axion clouds around spinning black holes, where superradiant instability piles ultralight bosons into clouds. Precise frequencies matter for catching these steady signals. Using relativistic perturbation theory built on a bilinear form, he treats self-interaction effects for the first time and revisits the self-gravity part. The result is a simple, unified framework for many excited modes at once, useful for next-generation gravitational-wave searches.
arxiv-2604-21539: Nihad Abuawwad and Samir Lounis review chiral spin textures in van der Waals stacks, where interfaces, strong spin-orbit coupling, and tunable symmetry breaking help stabilize chiral states. Skyrmions and textures draw interest for topology, chirality, tiny-scale stability, and spintronic promise. The review covers how they form, including exchange effects, anisotropy, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya effect, and dipolar effects, plus lab advances in seeing and handling them, their motion, transport signs, and theory. It closes with open challenges and next steps toward robust room-temperature textures for usable spintronic tech.
arxiv-2604-21739: Vlamidis and seven colleagues slip nickel beneath epitaxial graphene on silicon carbide, creating a two-dimensional magnetic stack for spintronic devices. Tiny nickel particles about 10 nanometres wide are laid down from a liquid bath at room temperature.
